doc: A process runtime.db recorded (what a crashed hub, or an older hub's Lisp backend, left: its own group, pid, start time and boot) is killed when the next hub starts, and the row goes. The row plants the record for a live process of its own group, left running by a shell that has gone (as a crashed hub's child is); a hub that finds the pid, the start time and the boot unchanged kills it within 4 s and says so in its log.

args: set -e; setsid sleep 300 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & p=$!; sleep 0.3; st=$(awk '{ sub(/^.*\) /, ""); print $20 }' /proc/$p/stat); boot=$(tr -d '\n' < /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id); printf '{"pid": %s, "st": %s, "boot": "%s"}' "$p" "$st" "$boot" > $ROOT/orphan.json

sql: insert into proc (purpose, pid, start_time, pgid, boot_id, at) values ('backend', $orphan, $st, $orphan, '$boot', 1.5)

contains: killed an orphan a crashed or older hub left
